outputs.exact_statement:
For every fixed real constant $A\ge1$, it is NP-hard to approximate minimum directed feedback vertex set within factor $A$ on unweighted digraphs. More precisely, there is a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from an NP-hard promise problem to instances $(G,k)$ with $k\in\mathbb N_{>0}$. The polynomial and its constants may depend on $A$. The reduction has the following alternatives: $$\textnormal{YES: }\mathop{\mathrm{DFVS}}(G)\le k,
  \qquad
  \textnormal{NO: }\mathop{\mathrm{DFVS}}(G)>Ak.$$

For every constant $\theta\in(0,1/2)$, there are constant label sets $X,Y$ such that it is $\mathrm{NP}$-hard, by a deterministic polynomial-time reduction, to distinguish two-to-one games of the following kinds:*

1.  *there is a labeling of value at least $1-\theta$;*

2.  *every labeling has value at most $\theta$.*

*Every constraint is a total map $X\to Y$ with exactly two preimages of each label in $Y$. The label sets may depend on $\theta$.

For every $b\ge0$ and $\alpha>0$, there is a finite integer $J_{\mathrm{unif}}(b,\alpha)$ with the following property. For every finite $S$ and every Boolean function $f:2^S\to\{0,1\}$ with $I_{1/2}(f)\le b$, there is a Boolean function $\widetilde f$, depending on at most $J_{\mathrm{unif}}(b,\alpha)$ coordinates, for which $$\Pr_{R\sim\mu_{1/2}^{S}}[\,f(R)\ne\widetilde f(R)\,]\le\alpha.$$ The bound is independent of $\lvert S\rvert$.

Let $p=2^{-k}$, where $k\ge1$ is an integer. For every $b\ge0$ and $\alpha>0$, there is a finite integer $J(p,b,\alpha)$, independent of $\lvert S\rvert$, such that every Boolean function $f:2^S\to\{0,1\}$ with $I_p(f)\le b$ has a Boolean junta approximant on at most $J(p,b,\alpha)$ coordinates with error at most $\alpha$ under $\mu_p^S$.

Every global game labeling $\ell$ gives a well-defined real value on the rank vertices by $$b_{\mathbf d}(x)\longmapsto x(\ell(\mathbf d)),$$ where $\ell(\mathbf d)$ is the tuple of labels supplied by $\ell$. Every rank arc strictly increases this value. Consequently, the rank graph has no self-loops, and $o_1,\ldots,o_N$ are distinct vertices with an arc $o_j\to o_{j'}$ whenever $j<j'$.
If the input game has a labeling satisfying a fraction at least $1-\theta$ of its constraints under $\nu$, then the constructed digraph has a feedback vertex set of cost at most $4$.

For each fixed $A$, the preceding construction produces a loopless digraph with positive rational vertex costs in deterministic polynomial time in the game input size. Its vertex costs are bounded above by a constant depending only on $A$.

For every integer $L\ge3$ and every $\eta>0$, there are an integer $N\ge L$ and a rational probability distribution on increasing maps $\psi\colon[L]\hookrightarrow[N]$ such that, for all $I,I'\in\binom{[L]}{3}$, $$\label{eq:rank-spreading-tv} \mathop{\mathrm{TV}}\bigl(\mathcal L(\psi(I)),\mathcal L(\psi(I'))\bigr)\le\eta.$$ Here $\mathcal L$ denotes the law of a random variable, and all the laws in Equation [eq:rank-spreading-tv] use the same random map $\psi$.

If $\mathbf d$ is good at $\psi$, then $g_{\mathbf d}\colon2^{\Lambda_{\mathbf d}}\to\{0,1\}$ is monotone: $$E\subseteq E'\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  g_{\mathbf d}(E)\le g_{\mathbf d}(E').$$ Moreover, $$g_{\mathbf d}(\varnothing)=0,
  \qquad g_{\mathbf d}(\Lambda_{\mathbf d})=1.$$

Under the common law of $(\mathcal D,e)$, for every $i\in[M]$, $$\mathbb Eh_u(p_i)\ge\frac{p_i}{4}.
  \label{eq:prefix-lower-bound}$$

Under the common law of $\mathcal D$ and an independent edge $e=(u,v)\sim\nu$, $$\mathbb E B_u\le D+1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E B_v\le D+1.
 \label{eq:pivotal-budget}$$

Suppose a game has value at most $\theta$. Assign to every game vertex $w$ a list $J_w\subseteq\Lambda_w$, possibly empty, of cardinality at most an integer $J\ge1$. Then $$\Pr_{e=(u,v)\sim\nu}
    [\,\pi_e(J_u)\cap J_v\ne\varnothing\,]\le\theta J^2.$$ The same conclusion holds conditionally on any data independent of the fresh edge, if all the lists are fixed by those data.

For every $i\in[M]$, under the common distribution of $(\mathcal D,e)$, $$\label{eq:product-comparison}
  \mathbb E\bigl[h_u(p_i)(1-h_v(q_i))\bigr]\le\frac{p_i}{16}.$$
If the game has value at most $\theta$, every feedback vertex set of the constructed weighted digraph has cost strictly greater than $D$.

Let $G$ be a loopless digraph on $S\ge1$ vertices with positive rational vertex costs $w_v\le C$. Set $c_v=\lceil Sw_v\rceil$. Replace every vertex $v$ by an independent set $\mathcal C_v$ of $c_v$ unweighted vertices, and replace every arc $u\to v$ by all arcs from $\mathcal C_u$ to $\mathcal C_v$. Call the resulting digraph $\widehat G$. Then $$\mathop{\mathrm{DFVS}}(\widehat G)
  =\min\left\{\sum_{v\in F}c_v:
      F\text{ is a feedback vertex set of }G\right\}.
  \label{eq:clone-exact-optimum}$$ The number of vertices of $\widehat G$ is at most $CS^2+S$. For fixed $C$, this is a deterministic polynomial construction in the encoding size of $G$ and its costs. Moreover:*

1.  *a feedback vertex set of $G$ of cost at most $a$ yields a feedback vertex set of $\widehat G$ of size at most $S(a+1)$;*

2.  *if every feedback vertex set of $G$ has cost greater than $b$, then $\mathop{\mathrm{DFVS}}(\widehat G)>Sb$.

For every fixed real $A\ge1$, approximating directed feedback arc set within factor $A$ is NP-hard on unweighted simple loopless digraphs. More precisely, there is a deterministic polynomial reduction producing such a digraph $H$ and a positive integer $k$ with the promise gap $$\begin{array}{ll}
    \text{YES:}&\operatorname{DFAS}(H)\le k,\\[2pt]
    \text{NO:}&\operatorname{DFAS}(H)>Ak.
  \end{array}$$

purpose: Constant-factor hardness of directed feedback vertex set

coverage.checked_domain: Exhaustive loopless simple digraphs on two and three vertices with unit clone multiplicities; all nine selected rational weight pairs on a directed two-cycle; singleton, mixed multiplicity, four-cycle, and eight-clone boundaries.
coverage.oracle_basis: Candidate enumerates clone deletion subsets with Kahn ordering; oracle enumerates original directed cycles and exact minimum hitting sets using Fraction, and independently rechecks the clone witness by recursion-stack cycle detection.
